author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Pager and navigator actions use anchors as custom buttons
findings.consequence: These controls are actions that mutate the current route, but they rely on duplicated role, tabindex, and keyboard handlers instead of native button semantics. That keeps the current UI keyboard-operable, but increases accessibility drift risk and already diverges from nearby button-based pager styling.
findings.evidence: Line 1784 renders `Gå till första träffen` as `<a role="button" tabindex="0">` with manual click/keyboard handlers; the same pattern is repeated for last page, goto-page toggle, and navigator facet actions in this owned template. Nearby previous/next pager actions use native `<button type="button">` on lines 1764 and 1773.
findings.recommendation: Render these route-mutating controls as `<button type="button">` elements with the same handlers and pressed/disabled state, preserving anchors only for real navigation links with `href`.
